summary: Review blocks manual simulator rerun until Builder fixes console-variable readback. The realistic-mode default/opt-out behavior is implemented and local project config supports on-demand RT, but the readback path can pass a null console-variable handle into SPEAR's C++ getter if any requested CVar is absent, which can assert/crash before the user gets useful logs.
work_completed: Read Builder result packet and reviewed diffs for examples/flashlight/run.py, examples/flashlight/flashlight_profiles.py, and tests/test_orbit_collection_validation.py.

Checked local Unreal project RT context in cpp/unreal_projects/SpearSim/Config/DefaultEngine.ini and SPEAR console-variable service bindings in cpp/unreal_plugins/SpServices/Source/SpServices/UnrealService.h.
Verified realistic live mode requests hardware RT by default and --disable-hardware-ray-tracing suppresses launch/runtime RT requests, while default live mode does not request RT.
Reviewed spotlight ray-traced shadow probing and new tests for coverage and brittleness.
Ran python -m unittest tests.test_orbit_collection_validation: 84 tests passed.
Ran python -m py_compile examples/flashlight/run.py examples/flashlight/flashlight_profiles.py tests/test_orbit_collection_validation.py successfully.

findings.message: Blocker: examples/flashlight/run.py:522 only treats None as a missing console variable, but SPEAR's C++ find_console_variable_by_name binding returns a uint64_t pointer value and returns 0 when IConsoleManager::FindConsoleVariable is missing (cpp/unreal_plugins/SpServices/Source/SpServices/UnrealService.h:1204-1207). If any requested RT/Lumen CVar is unsupported, try_read_console_variable_int will call get_console_variable_value_as_int(cvar=0); the getter asserts on a null cvar (UnrealService.h:1215-1218), so the simulator can crash during readback. Remediation: treat falsy/0 handles as missing before calling getters, and add a test where find_console_variable_by_name returns 0.

examples/flashlight/flashlight_profiles.py:360-377 can report ray-traced shadow intent applied after the first successful call with True. Unreal's SetCastRaytracedShadow/property is enum-shaped, so True may map to UseProjectSetting rather than Enabled, and the code returns before trying 'Enabled' or 2. Remediation: prefer the explicit enabled enum/string/integer candidates before bool, or verify readback equals the enabled value before marking applied.

tests/test_orbit_collection_validation.py:844-872 only covers the all-CVars-present happy path for runtime readback, and tests/test_orbit_collection_validation.py:687-710 only covers bool-accepting fake shadow setters/properties. The tests miss the null-handle crash path and the enum-valued shadow path that are most relevant to the runtime risk.

The launch/runtime request behavior itself matches the task: realistic live mode appends r.RayTracing.Enable=1 and Lumen hardware RT CVars by default, --disable-hardware-ray-tracing suppresses them, and default live mode does not request RT. Local SpearSim config already has r.RayTracing=True, r.SkinCache.CompileShaders=True, r.RayTracing.EnableOnDemand=1, and DX12 Windows target settings, so r.RayTracing.Enable=1 is coherent with existing project intent.

follow_up_recommendations: Builder should fix try_read_console_variable_int to handle cvar is None or cvar == 0 before invoking any getter, then add regression coverage for a 0 handle and for missing/unsupported CVars returning confirmed=false or null without crashing.

Builder should adjust ray-traced spotlight shadow probing to avoid a false applied state for enum properties, ideally by trying explicit enabled values first and logging readback comparison where available.
After those fixes, rerun python -m unittest tests.test_orbit_collection_validation and py_compile before the user reruns the simulator.
memory_worthy: Hardware RT flashlight review found a blocker: console-variable readback must treat SPEAR's 0 console-variable handle as missing before calling C++ getters, or unsupported CVars can assert/crash the simulator.
